tools.problem: Labels and FDA-PH registration demand a best-before/expiry date, but MSMEs guess it; when a product spoils early or an auditor asks for the basis, they have no stability study to stand behind the number.
tools.who: Packaged-food, bakery, beverage and sauce/pickle manufacturers who must put a defensible best-before date on a label.
tools.solution: Set up real-time or accelerated studies with scheduled pull points, log organoleptic, pH/water-activity and micro results at each interval against limits, and have the tool derive and date-stamp the supportable shelf life with an exportable study report to file with the dossier.
tools.regulation: FSSAI Labelling & Display Regulations (best-before basis); FDA-PH product stability requirement

tools.title: Tingi / Repack Bulk-Break Pricing
tools.problem: Owners guess the per-piece price when breaking a bulk pack, ignoring packaging, spillage/weight-loss and odd-paisa/centavo rounding, so the tingi margin they think they earn quietly evaporates.
tools.who: Sari-sari (PH) and kirana/provision (IN) owners who buy bulk and sell in small tingi/loose portions — sachets split from a dozen, rice/sugar/oil repacked from a sack, single sticks from a pack.
tools.solution: Enter the bulk buy (pack size, cost, free goods) and the repack unit; the app computes true per-tingi cost after a wastage %, suggests a clean sell price at a target margin, shows margin at common price points, and prints small repack labels with net quantity.
tools.regulation: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules 2011 net-quantity declaration (IN)

tools.title: Van Sales Load-Out & Settlement
tools.problem: Morning van stock, through-day sales, free goods, breakages and end-of-day returns rarely tally with the cash and credit brought back, and shortages surface days later with no proof.
tools.who: FMCG sub-distributors and wholesalers running cash/delivery vans (DSD) where the salesman sells and delivers from van stock on the spot.
tools.solution: Load the van by SKU in the morning; the salesman bills each outlet from van stock (cash or credit) on the phone; at day-end the app reconciles loaded minus sold minus returned against a physical van count, and cash collected against sales, flagging every gap by SKU and by outlet.

tools.title: Market Return & Expiry Claim to Company
tools.problem: Returns pile up in the godown in loose cartons; by the time a claim reaches the company, expiry windows have closed and half the value is written off, with no batch-level proof.
tools.who: FMCG distributors/sub-stockists whose field team pulls near-expiry, damaged and saleable returns from retailers and must recover credit from the principal company.
tools.solution: Field team logs each return at the outlet (SKU, batch, expiry, reason, photo); the app batches returns into a company-wise claim within the policy window, prints the gate-pass/debit note, and tracks it to the credit note the company actually issues.
tools.regulation: GST credit note, Sec 34 CGST Act (IN); FSSAI/FDA date-expiry handling

tools.title: Supplier Price Compare (Landed)
tools.problem: The cheapest source changes week to week once schemes, free goods, delivery and credit terms are counted, but owners can't hold five price lists in their head and overpay on staples.
tools.who: Kirana/sari-sari and small self-service grocers who buy the same SKUs from several sources — local distributor, cash-and-carry and B2B apps (Udaan/Metro/GrowSari).
tools.solution: Keep each supplier's price, scheme and delivery per SKU; the tool shows the true landed price from each source side by side and builds a split buy-list that routes each SKU to its cheapest supplier this week.

tools.title: Jewellery Stock + HUID & Making-Charge Biller
tools.problem: Each bill is a manual sum of live metal rate times net weight plus making charges plus GST, and every hallmarked piece must carry its six-digit HUID — easy to misquote and non-compliant on paper.
tools.who: Small gold and silver jewellers billing by weight with making charges and mandatory hallmarking.
tools.solution: Maintain pieces by purity, gross/net weight and HUID; at billing, pull the day's metal rate and compute rate times weight plus making (per-gram or flat) plus GST plus hallmarking, then print a compliant tax invoice with the HUID on it; stock stays valued at today's rate.
tools.regulation: BIS Hallmarking (HUID) mandatory; GST on jewellery (IN)

tools.title: BC/AePS Agent Till & Commission
tools.problem: The owner juggles an e-value wallet and the cash drawer across cash-outs, deposits and bill payments; float runs dry mid-day and the commission actually earned is a mystery.
tools.who: Village and small-town kiranas doubling as Banking Correspondent / AePS cash-out and BBPS bill-payment points.
tools.solution: Log each AePS withdrawal/deposit, DMT and BBPS bill-pay; the till tracks e-value float vs cash-in-drawer in real time, warns before float runs out, computes commission per service, nets GST, and closes the day with a cash-vs-wallet tally.
tools.regulation: RBI Business Correspondent framework; NPCI AePS; BBPS (IN)

tools.title: Agri-Drone Spray Service Log & Billing
tools.problem: Operators spray dozens of fields a day for hire but track sorties, chemical used, area and payments on paper; they cannot prove sprayed acreage to a farmer who disputes the bill, and they keep nothing like the sortie/chemical log that DGCA and agri-department subsidy audits expect.
tools.who: Independent kisan-drone spray operators and drone entrepreneurs (including Namo Drone Didi SHGs) who spray farmers' fields on hire.
tools.solution: A field app that starts a sortie, captures the GPS-walked field boundary and sprayed area, the registered agrochemical, dose and tank mixes, battery-per-acre and the farmer, then produces a per-field per-acre bill plus a running sortie-and-chemical logbook ready for DGCA/subsidy records; works offline and syncs later.
tools.regulation: DGCA UAS Rules 2021 / CIB&RC drone-application SOP; SMAM agri-drone subsidy records

tools.title: Poultry Batch FCR & Contract-Grower Settlement Ledger
tools.problem: A grower's profit lives or dies on feed conversion and mortality, but they reconcile chick placement, daily feed bags, mortality and the integrator's settlement sheet by hand - and rarely catch when the integrator mis-states FCR, feed recovery or the growing charge.
tools.who: Independent broiler/layer farmers and small contract-growers tied to integrators (NECC/private).
tools.solution: Record placement (chicks, breed), daily feed, mortality and weights per batch, auto-compute live FCR, mortality % and batch P&L, then reconstruct the contract settlement (feed-cost recovery, growing charge per kg, FCR incentive/penalty) so the grower can check the integrator's payout to the last rupee or peso.

tools.title: Aquaculture Pond Feed & Water-Quality Log
tools.problem: Pond outcomes turn on feed discipline and water parameters, and antibiotic misuse gets whole export lots rejected - yet farmers keep feed, dissolved-oxygen/pH/salinity and any medication on scraps of paper, with no withdrawal-period record a processor or authority will accept.
tools.who: Small shrimp/fish pond farmers and lease operators (Andhra/Odisha; BFAR-registered ponds in the Philippines).
tools.solution: A pond-side offline app to log daily feed, DO/pH/salinity/ammonia, water exchange, inputs and any antibiotic with its withdrawal clock, per pond per crop; it warns when a planned harvest falls inside a withdrawal period and exports a per-pond input-and-residue history for the processor/CAA audit.
tools.regulation: Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA) registration (IN) / BFAR registration (PH); CAA antibiotic ban & seafood-export MRL

tools.title: Sugarcane Supply-Ticket & FRP Payment Tracker
tools.problem: A grower delivers cane all season against mill permits/calendars, but reconciling each supply ticket's weight, the mill's running account and whether the Fair & Remunerative Price was paid inside the 14-day legal window is near-impossible on paper - and overdue-payment interest claims go unmade.
tools.who: Cane-growing farmers and village cane-supply secretaries delivering to sugar mills.
tools.solution: Record each cane-supply permit and delivery (gross/tare/net, variety), accrue the amount due at the notified FRP/SAP, match mill payments against it, and flag any supply unpaid past 14 days with the interest then due - producing a clean grower-vs-mill statement.
tools.regulation: Sugarcane (Control) Order 1966 - FRP + 14-day payment & interest

tools.title: SRA Quedan & Sugar-Quota Allocation Tracker
tools.problem: Philippine raw sugar is classified and allocated by the SRA into A/B/C/D quotas and traded as quedans (warehouse receipts), and planters juggle allocation percentages, liens and quedan sales on paper, losing track of entitlements and sale proceeds.
tools.who: Sugarcane planters and small mill-district traders in the Philippines.
tools.solution: Track each milling's production, the SRA's quota classification and percentage split, quedans held (by class, mill, quantity), liens/assignments and quedan sales, giving the planter a live picture of sugar owned by class and its realizable value.
tools.regulation: Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) quedan & A/B/C/D quota system

tools.title: National Permit Multi-State Authorization Tracker
tools.problem: A Goods Carriage National Permit needs an annual composite authorization fee and stays valid only in states whose authorization is paid; drivers get detained at check-posts when a state's authorization has lapsed, and owners track the per-state paid-until dates nowhere.
tools.who: Goods-carriage fleet owners and transport managers running National Permit trucks across state borders.
tools.solution: Per-truck National Permit register holding the 5-year permit and the annual authorization, plus a state-by-state grid of paid-until dates; reminders before the annual authorization and any planned route's states lapse, with Parivahan/VAHAN payment deep-links and a border-readiness check for a chosen route.
tools.regulation: Goods Carriage National Permit, CMVR Rule 87 (authorization fee)

tools.title: Inbound Freight-Bill Audit & 3-Way Match (Rate-LR-POD)
tools.problem: Shippers agree lane rates (per-ton/per-km/fixed) but transporters' monthly freight bills quietly diverge (wrong rate, inflated weight, duplicate LR numbers, missing PODs) and staff approve them blind, overpaying and risking ITC on unmatched e-way bills.
tools.who: Manufacturers, distributors and traders who hire transporters and pay monthly freight bills.
tools.solution: Load the agreed rate contract per transporter/lane, import or key the freight bills and LRs, and auto 3-way match every bill line to its contracted rate and its delivered LR/POD; flag rate variances, over-weight, duplicate/missing LRs and missing PODs, and emit an approved-for-payment statement listing the disputed lines.
tools.regulation: GST ITC (freight invoice + e-way bill matching)

tools.title: FASTag Toll Reconciliation & Overcharge Dispute Builder
tools.problem: FASTag deductions arrive as an opaque bank/issuer feed; double deductions at a plaza, wrong vehicle-class (higher-axle) charges and tag misreads leak money, and owners can neither attribute toll to a truck/trip nor assemble the NHAI dispute.
tools.who: Fleet owners running several FASTag-fitted trucks.
tools.solution: Import the FASTag/bank statement (CSV), map each transaction to a vehicle and trip, auto-flag duplicate deductions inside a short window, wrong-class charges and unknown plazas, and generate a plaza-wise dispute note; monthly toll cost per truck and per trip for costing.
tools.regulation: NHAI FASTag / NPCI NETC

tools.title: Vehicle e-Challan & Fine-Settlement Tracker
tools.problem: Trucks silently accumulate e-challans (overspeed, overload, no-entry, PUC); unpaid ones block FC/permit renewal and drift to Virtual Court/Lok Adalat, and owners discover them only when a renewal fails, with no way to decide which fines a driver should bear.
tools.who: Fleet owners and transport managers.
tools.solution: Track e-challans per vehicle (keyed from the Parivahan e-Challan lookup), record violation, amount, driver at fault and payment status, net driver-fault fines into the driver's account, and warn before any FC/permit renewal that pending challans will block it, with Virtual Court payment deep-links.
tools.regulation: Motor Vehicles Act e-Challan (Parivahan), Virtual Courts

tools.title: Hamali Loading-Gang Tally & Wage Register
tools.problem: Loading-unloading labour is paid per bag/per ton/per truck across many jobs a day; tallying who loaded what, computing piece-rate wages and advances, and (in board states) the Mathadi levy and register is all manual and dispute-prone.
tools.who: Transport godowns, mandis and warehouses that use loading/unloading labour (hamal/mathadi gangs).
tools.solution: Log each loading/unloading job (truck, bags/tonnage, gang), compute piece-rate wages per hamal with advances and deductions, produce the daily gang wage sheet, and where applicable compute the Mathadi Board levy and keep the statutory register.
tools.regulation: Maharashtra Mathadi, Hamal and Other Manual Workers Act 1969 (and sister Hamali-board laws)

tools.title: Part-Load Booking & To-Pay Freight Register
tools.problem: Part-load agents consolidate many small consignments onto shared trucks and live on registers: which consignment sits on which truck, which freight is to-pay (collected at the destination branch) versus paid, and whether the destination branch actually collected and delivered.
tools.who: Part-load/LTL transport booking offices and parcel-booking agents moving godown-to-godown.
tools.solution: Book each part-load consignment (parties, articles, weight, paid/to-pay freight), build the truck loading sheet/trip challan that consolidates consignments, and track arrival and delivery at the destination branch with to-pay collection and a branch-wise booking plus outstanding-to-pay register.
tools.regulation: Carriage by Road Act 2007 (consignment note, carrier liability)

tools.title: Road Hazmat TREM Card & Compliance Pack
tools.problem: Hazmat road movement requires a TREM (transport emergency) card, a driver with the hazardous-goods endorsement/training, correct class placards and a per-trip document set under CMVR Rules 129-137; any slip means heavy penalty, impounding and a voided insurance claim.
tools.who: Transporters and tankers carrying dangerous/hazardous goods by road (chemicals, LPG, fuel, paints).
tools.solution: Generate the TREM card per UN number/consignment from a built-in dangerous-goods table, maintain each driver's hazmat endorsement and training expiry, give the placard/label checklist for the class, and assemble a per-trip hazmat document pack as a PDF.
tools.regulation: Central Motor Vehicles Rules, Rules 129-137 (carriage of dangerous goods); TREM card

tools.title: Metro Manila Truck Ban & Window-Hour Dispatch Planner
tools.problem: Trucks are barred from major roads during window hours that differ city by city (Manila, Makati, QC and more); a mistimed run means apprehension or impounding, and dispatchers juggle these schedules plus truck-ban exemption permits from memory.
tools.who: Trucking operators and dispatchers delivering into Metro Manila and other ban-enforcing LGUs.
tools.solution: A maintained city-by-city truck-ban schedule; enter the delivery city, truck weight class and desired arrival and it returns the allowed dispatch/arrival windows and the next clear slot, and it tracks each truck's exemption-permit validity.
tools.regulation: MMDA / LGU truck-ban ordinances; truck-ban exemption permits

tools.title: Inter-Island Cargo Booking & All-In Freight Cost Sheet
tools.problem: Coastal cargo means juggling per-line rates, voyage cutoffs, bills of lading and consignee pickup, while the true landed cost (freight plus arrastre, wharfage and trucking at both ends) is opaque, so shippers underquote and bookings live in chat threads.
tools.who: PH MSME shippers and small forwarders sending boxes/pallets/LCL cargo island-to-island by RORO and coastal lines.
tools.solution: A per-shipment booking register (line, vessel/voyage, cutoff, BL number, status to consignee pickup) with a reusable per-line/route rate card and an all-in cost sheet that adds freight, arrastre, wharfage and both-end trucking.
tools.regulation: PPA arrastre/wharfage; domestic bill of lading

tools.title: Merchant Export 0.1% GST Concessional-Procurement Tracker
tools.problem: Notification 40/2017-CT(R) and 41/2017-IGST(R) let a merchant exporter procure at 0.1% GST, but only if strict conditions hold - order placed on the supplier's GSTIN with a copy to the supplier's jurisdictional officer, goods moved directly to port/ICD, and export completed within 90 days of the supplier's tax invoice; miss any and the concession is denied with interest.
tools.who: Merchant exporters buying finished goods from domestic suppliers for export.
tools.solution: For each 0.1% procurement, generate the compliant purchase order and the intimation to the jurisdictional officer, start a 90-day export clock, link the shipping bill/EGM proof when exported, and flag any procurement nearing day 90 without an export against it.
tools.regulation: Notification 40/2017-Central Tax (Rate); 41/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate)

tools.title: PH Export-Sales VAT Zero-Rating Substantiation & Refund Pack
tools.problem: Export sales are zero-rated under NIRC Sec 106(A)(2)/108(B), but to defend the 0% in a BIR audit and claim a refund of input VAT under Sec 112, the exporter must prove the export with a matched set - sales invoice, export declaration/bill of lading, and proof of inward foreign-currency remittance - which MSMEs assemble haphazardly and then lose the refund.
tools.who: Philippine exporters whose sales are VAT zero-rated and who accumulate input VAT.
tools.solution: Build one evidence bundle per export sale (zero-rated sales invoice, export declaration, BL/AWB, bank inward-remittance credit), reconcile the peso amounts across them, compute the input VAT attributable to zero-rated sales, and output the Sec 112 refund application packet with its substantiation schedule.
tools.regulation: NIRC Sec 106(A)(2), 108(B) (zero-rating) and Sec 112 (VAT refund)

tools.title: Pre-Shipment Inspection & Certificate-of-Conformity Coordinator
tools.problem: Many destinations block goods at the port of entry without a pre-shipment Certificate of Conformity - Nigeria's SONCAP, Kenya's PVoC, Saudi SABER/SASO and similar - each with its own route (product registration, test reports, physical inspection); MSMEs discover the requirement only after the buyer's goods are stuck and pay demurrage.
tools.who: Exporters shipping to African and Middle-East markets that enforce destination conformity assessment.
tools.solution: Enter product (HS) and destination to get the exact scheme, route (registration vs batch inspection vs licensing), required test reports and accredited bodies; then manage the file per shipment - book the inspection, upload test reports, and track issuance of the CoC before the vessel sails.
tools.regulation: SONCAP (Nigeria); PVoC (Kenya, KEBS); SABER/SASO (Saudi Arabia)

tools.title: Export Health Certificate & Inspection Organizer (EIC/EIA, BFAR/FDA)
tools.problem: Markets like the EU require an official Health Certificate for products of animal origin, issued in India by the Export Inspection Council/Agencies under the Export (Quality Control and Inspection) Act, 1963, and in the Philippines by BFAR/FDA; MSMEs miss sampling windows, let establishment approvals lapse, and ship without the certificate the destination border demands.
tools.who: Exporters of fish, marine, dairy, egg, honey and processed animal products needing a government health certificate.
tools.solution: Track establishment/plant approval numbers and their validity, schedule the pre-shipment sampling and lab tests the certificate requires, generate the health-certificate application per consignment, and store issued certificates against each shipping bill/export declaration.
tools.regulation: Export (Quality Control and Inspection) Act, 1963 (EIC/EIA); BFAR/FDA-PH health certification

tools.title: Packing Credit & Interest-Equalisation Export-Finance Tracker
tools.problem: Pre-shipment packing credit (and PCFC) is advanced against confirmed orders/LCs and must be liquidated out of export proceeds within the sanctioned period; MSMEs lose track of drawing power against each order, risk overdue liquidation (which converts to costly ordinary interest), and fail to claim the Interest Equalisation Scheme subvention they are entitled to.
tools.who: Small exporters funding production with pre- and post-shipment export credit.
tools.solution: Track each packing-credit drawing against its order/LC, monitor drawing power and the liquidation deadline, match export proceeds/BRCs to liquidate the right advance, and compute the IES interest subvention due per account for the bank claim.
tools.regulation: RBI export credit (packing credit/PCFC); Interest Equalisation Scheme (IES)

tools.title: GST Common-Credit ITC Reversal Calculator (Rule 42/43)
tools.problem: When turnover is a mix of taxable and exempt supply, common input-tax credit must be apportioned and partly reversed every month under Rule 42, with an annual true-up and a 60-month capital-goods reversal under Rule 43. The formula (D1/D2, T4) is error-prone and a wrong figure invites ITC-recovery demands with interest.
tools.who: Small manufacturers, traders, clinics, builders and agri-traders making both taxable and exempt/nil-rated supplies.
tools.solution: Enter total ITC, exempt vs taxable turnover and the capital-goods list; it computes the monthly Rule 42 reversal, the Rule 43 capital-goods reversal over 60 months and the year-end true-up, producing an auditable working with the exact GSTR-3B Table 4(B) figures to key in.
tools.regulation: CGST Rules 42 & 43

tools.title: Rule 37 Unpaid-Supplier ITC Reversal & Reclaim Tracker
tools.problem: If a buyer does not pay a supplier within 180 days of invoice, the ITC already claimed must be reversed with interest under the second proviso to Sec 16(2)/Rule 37, and reclaimed only once paid. Almost no micro-firm tracks the 180-day clock per invoice and they get caught in audit.
tools.who: MSMEs that stretch supplier payments and claim ITC on purchases — trading, construction and job-work chains.
tools.solution: Import the purchase register; it runs a 180-day countdown per invoice, flags credits due for reversal, computes the interest, generates the GSTR-3B reversal entry and auto-reinstates the credit in the month payment is recorded.
tools.regulation: CGST Sec 16(2) second proviso & Rule 37

tools.title: QRMP Optimizer & IFF B2B Upload Helper
tools.problem: QRMP taxpayers must decide each month whether to pay via the fixed-sum 35% challan or self-assessment, and whether to push B2B invoices into the Invoice Furnishing Facility in months 1 and 2 so buyers get ITC. Most either overpay the 35% challan or strand their buyers' credit by skipping IFF.
tools.who: Small GST taxpayers with turnover up to Rs 5 crore on the Quarterly Return Monthly Payment scheme.
tools.solution: Enter the quarter's sales and last period's liability; it recommends the monthly PMT-06 amount (fixed-sum vs self-assessment), flags which B2B invoices to file in IFF within the Rs 50-lakh cap, and lays out the interest-safe GSTR-1/3B quarterly calendar.
tools.regulation: GST QRMP scheme / Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) / Form PMT-06

tools.title: 194Q vs 206C(1H) Buyer/Seller TDS-TCS Decider & Ledger
tools.problem: On high-value goods the law overlaps: the buyer may owe 0.1% TDS under Sec 194Q while the seller may owe 0.1% TCS under Sec 206C(1H), and 194Q takes precedence. Both sides routinely double-tax or miss it, then fight 26AS mismatches.
tools.who: Traders, manufacturers and wholesalers with any customer or supplier crossing Rs 50 lakh of goods a year.
tools.solution: Enter the counterparty's turnover bracket and the running value of goods traded; it decides who must deduct/collect, from which rupee the Rs 50-lakh threshold bites, the correct rate (incl. no-PAN 5%/1%), and keeps a per-party ledger with the amount to deduct on the next invoice.
tools.regulation: Income-tax Sec 194Q & Sec 206C(1H)

tools.title: GST Place-of-Supply & IGST-vs-CGST/SGST Determiner
tools.problem: Charging IGST when it should be CGST+SGST (or vice-versa) is one of the commonest GST errors and is hard to undo — the buyer loses ITC and the seller faces re-payment. Rules differ for goods, services, bill-to-ship-to, transport, events and OIDAR.
tools.who: Freelancers, service firms and traders invoicing across state lines, and anyone handling bill-to/ship-to orders.
tools.solution: A short wizard (supply type, supplier state, recipient/registration, delivery or performance location) applies the IGST Act Sec 10-13 rules to return the place of supply and whether to charge IGST or CGST+SGST, with the governing section cited for the invoice file.
tools.regulation: IGST Act Sec 10-13 (place of supply)

tools.title: Payment-Gateway Settlement Reconciler
tools.problem: Gateways settle on T+1/T+2 net of MDR, GST-on-fees, refunds and chargebacks, in batches that never line up 1:1 with orders. Owners can't tell if they were actually paid for each order, or spot a short-settled or held payout.
tools.who: Online sellers and D2C/service MSMEs collecting via Razorpay/Cashfree/PayU (IN) or PayMongo/Xendit/Maya (PH)
tools.solution: Import the gateway settlement/payout report plus the order export; it matches payout lines to orders, reconstructs each order's fee/tax/refund/chargeback, flags unsettled, short-settled, held and double-refunded transactions, and books the net to a bank-ready journal with the MDR and GST-on-MDR split out for ITC.
tools.regulation: RBI Payment Aggregator/PG Guidelines (IN); BSP Operations of Payment Systems rules (PH)

tools.title: PDC & Cheque Register with Deposit Scheduler
tools.problem: Post-dated cheques pile up in a drawer; owners miss deposit dates, deposit too early and get a dishonour, or lose track of which issued PDC will hit the bank and sink the balance.
tools.who: B2B MSMEs that still receive and issue post-dated cheques (traders, distributors, contractors)
tools.solution: Log every PDC received and issued (party, bank, cheque no., amount, due date); it builds a deposit calendar, warns before an issued cheque will overdraw the account, tracks clearance/bounce status, and on a bounce pre-fills the Sec 138 / BP 22 notice timeline and hands off to litigation tracking.
tools.regulation: Negotiable Instruments Act Sec 138 (IN); Batas Pambansa Blg. 22 (PH)

tools.title: CMA Data Builder (bank working-capital / term-loan)
tools.problem: Banks demand CMA (Credit Monitoring Arrangement) data, audited past plus projected financials, ratios and an MPBF working-capital assessment, in a rigid format. MSMEs pay consultants 5,000 to 25,000 per file or get rejected for a sloppy one.
tools.who: MSMEs applying for or renewing a bank CC/OD or term loan, and the consultants who prepare their files
tools.solution: Guided entry of 2-3 past years plus projections generates the standard CMA Forms (operating statement, balance-sheet analysis, comparative current assets/liabilities, MPBF, fund-flow, ratios), auto-computes MPBF (Tandon/Nayak Method II), current ratio, DSCR and TOL/TNW, and exports a bank-ready workbook plus PDF.
tools.regulation: RBI CMA / Maximum Permissible Bank Finance (Tandon-Nayak norms)

tools.title: Drawing Power & Monthly Stock-Statement Generator
tools.problem: CC/OD borrowers must submit a monthly stock and book-debt statement; drawing power is (paid stock + eligible debtors - creditors) less the bank's margin. Get it wrong and the account is flagged irregular; do it by hand monthly and it eats a day.
tools.who: MSMEs running a cash-credit (CC) or overdraft limit against stock and book debts
tools.solution: Enter or import stock, debtors (with aging cut-off) and creditors; it applies the sanction's margins, excludes slow/over-90-day debtors and unpaid stock, computes drawing power vs sanctioned limit, warns if utilisation will breach DP, and prints the bank's stock-statement format.
tools.regulation: RBI cash-credit drawing-power / stock & book-debt statement norms

tools.title: MSME Multi-Loan Debt-Stack & Payoff Planner
tools.problem: With 4-5 borrowings at different rates and EMIs, owners don't know their true blended cost, which loan to kill first, or whether a prepayment or refinance actually helps after foreclosure charges.
tools.who: Owner-operators juggling several loans (term loan, CC, equipment finance, gold loan, business BNPL, informal)
tools.solution: Enter every loan (principal, rate, EMI, tenor, foreclosure terms); it shows blended APR and total interest outgo, ranks payoff by avalanche vs snowball, simulates a lump-sum prepayment or a consolidation/refinance offer net of foreclosure charges, and gives a month-by-month payoff plan.

tools.title: Inward-Remittance Channel Cost Comparator
tools.problem: The same $2,000 from a foreign client lands as wildly different amounts via SWIFT bank wire vs Wise vs PayPal vs Payoneer, through hidden FX markup, flat fees, GST on forex and purpose-code friction, yet nobody compares before sharing payment details.
tools.who: Freelancers, IT/service exporters and small exporters receiving foreign-currency payments
tools.solution: Enter amount, currency and corridor; it computes the true landed amount on each channel (mid-market rate minus each provider's FX markup, plus fixed/percentage fees and, for India, GST on forex plus likely FIRC/eBRC availability for the GST export refund), ranks them, and generates the payment instructions to send the client.
tools.regulation: FEMA purpose codes / FIRC-eBRC (IN); BSP inward-remittance rules (PH)

tools.title: PH MSME Loan-Program & Microfinance Matcher
tools.problem: PH micro-entrepreneurs don't know which public and microfinance options they qualify for, DTI P3 (Pondo sa Pagbabago), SB Corp, LANDBANK/DBP MSME windows, RSBSA-linked agri credit or an accredited MFI, and default to 5-6 informal lenders at punishing rates.
tools.who: Philippine micro and small entrepreneurs seeking formal credit
tools.solution: A wizard: business type, DTI/BMBE status, location, years operating, amount and purpose returns a ranked list of eligible programs with ceilings, rates, collateral-free limits, required documents and the office/MFI to approach, plus the true-cost gap vs the 5-6 lender they'd otherwise use.
tools.regulation: RA 6977/9501 (Magna Carta for MSMEs); DTI P3 & SB Corp program rules; BMBE Act (RA 9178)

tools.title: GST Inverted-Duty Refund (Rule 89(5)) Calculator & RFD-01 Pack
tools.problem: When inputs carry higher GST than the finished good, unutilised ITC piles up as trapped cash. The Rule 89(5) refund formula, with its recurring circular tweaks, is complex, so MSMEs either don't claim or get rejected.
tools.who: MSMEs in textiles, footwear, fertilizer, EV, utensils and other inverted-duty trades (inputs taxed higher than output)
tools.solution: Enter period turnover, tax rates, inward ITC split (inputs vs input-services/capital goods) and adjusted total turnover; it computes Maximum Refund per the current Rule 89(5) formula, shows the claimable amount, builds Statement 1/1A and the RFD-01 support pack, and tracks claims filed vs sanctioned.
tools.regulation: CGST Rule 89(5) (inverted duty structure); Form RFD-01 / Statement 1A

tools.title: PH Pawnshop (Sangla) Loan & Redemption Manager
tools.problem: Pawnshops run a lending book on paper (pawn tickets, appraised collateral, accruing interest, grace periods, renewals, auction of unredeemed items), which is error-prone and hard to keep PD 114 / BSP compliant.
tools.who: Neighbourhood pawnshop (sangla) owners and small lending-investor MSMEs
tools.solution: Issue each pawn ticket (item photo, appraisal, principal, rate, maturity + grace), accrue interest and penalties to date, handle renewals and partial payments, flag items past grace for auction, and keep the compliant register with daily cash position and the ticket's required disclosures.
tools.regulation: PD 114 (Pawnshop Regulation Act); BSP MORNBFI rules

tools.title: PM Vishwakarma Enrollment & Benefit Tracker
tools.problem: PM Vishwakarma is a trade-eligibility gate followed by a multi-stage benefit chain: certificate+ID, 5-7 day basic skilling with a Rs500/day stipend, a Rs15,000 toolkit e-voucher, a Rs1 lakh then Rs2 lakh collateral-free loan at 5%, and a Rs1/transaction digital incentive. Artisans never know which stage they are at, what unlocks next, or why a benefit has stalled.
tools.who: Individual artisans in the 18 PM Vishwakarma trades (potters, carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, cobblers, basket/mat weavers, toy-makers, etc.) and the CSC VLEs or NGO facilitators who enroll them.
tools.solution: A per-artisan enrollment-to-benefit pipeline: a trade-eligibility and exclusion check (e.g. income-tax payers and govt employees are out), a document pre-fill for the CSC biometric enrollment, then a stage tracker recording certificate/ID issue, skilling completion, toolkit-voucher redemption, each loan tranche, and digital-transaction incentive accrual, surfacing the next action and missing document for every artisan.
tools.regulation: PM Vishwakarma Scheme (Ministry of MSME)

tools.title: BIS Hallmarking (HUID) Register for Small Jewelers
tools.problem: Under the HUID mandate every gold article sold must carry a 6-digit HUID and only hallmarked stock is legal, yet small jewelers juggle items sent to the Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC), items returned with HUIDs, and legacy non-HUID stock with no per-piece record for BIS market-sampling or a consumer complaint.
tools.who: Small goldsmiths, karigars and single-counter jewelers operating in mandatory-hallmarking districts.
tools.solution: A per-piece hallmarking register: log each article with purity (14/18/20/22/23/24K), weight and photo, group them into AHC submission lots, record the HUID and hallmark returned, flag hallmarked-vs-pending-vs-legacy stock, and keep the trail BIS or a customer complaint would demand, including the purity/caratage disclosure at point of sale.
tools.regulation: BIS Act 2016 + Hallmarking Regulations (mandatory HUID)

tools.title: Precious-Material Issue-&-Return Weight Ledger
tools.problem: Gold, silver and zari thread are issued to karigars by weight and must come back as finished weight plus scrap within an allowed wastage, but without a tight weight ledger shortage and pilferage hide inside 'wastage' and disputes with karigars become unresolvable.
tools.who: Jewelry karkhanas, goldsmith and silversmith units, and zari/zardozi workshops that hand out precious material to karigars.
tools.solution: An issue-and-return weight ledger: record material issued to each karigar by weight and purity, the finished-piece weight and returned scrap, the agreed wastage percentage, and auto-compute the shortage/excess per job and per karigar, with a running balance of material out with each worker.

tools.title: Craft Fair & Exhibition Application Tracker
tools.problem: Income depends on getting into the right fairs, but each has its own application deadline, juried-submission requirement, stall fee and document list; makers miss deadlines, double-book dates, and never learn which fairs actually paid off.
tools.who: Artisans, D2C craft brands and cooperatives who work the juried craft-fair circuit (Dilli Haat, Dastkar, Surajkund, Manila FAME, Sikat Pinoy, OTOP fairs).
tools.solution: A fair-circuit tracker: a calendar of fairs with application windows, stall fees and jury/sample requirements, a per-fair application status (applied/accepted/waitlisted/paid), date-clash warnings, and a post-fair ROI log (sales and leads vs stall and travel cost) that ranks fairs for next season.

tools.title: Artisan Design Copyright & Anti-Copy Kit
tools.problem: Design theft is rampant and makers have no dated proof of first creation and no idea how to register a design or push back, so copies undercut them with impunity.
tools.who: Original-design artisans and small craft studios whose patterns, motifs and product designs get copied on marketplaces.
tools.solution: A design-protection kit: a timestamped, hash-sealed portfolio that logs each design with creation date and evidence, guidance on registering under the Designs Act / Copyright (India) or IPOPHL (Philippines), and a generator for marketplace takedown notices and cease-and-desist letters citing the maker's dated record.
tools.regulation: Designs Act 2000 / Copyright Act 1957 (IN); IP Code RA 8293 / IPOPHL (PH)

tools.title: Corporate Craft Gifting Quote & Hamper Builder
tools.problem: Corporate gifting is the highest-value craft channel but artisans quote it badly, assembling custom hampers, tiered bulk pricing, branding add-ons and multi-address delivery by hand, and lose orders to slow, unprofessional quotes.
tools.who: Craft makers and D2C brands chasing corporate bulk-gifting orders (Diwali/Christmas hampers, event giveaways, onboarding kits).
tools.solution: A hamper configurator and quote builder: compose a gift box from craft SKUs with packaging, add logo/custom-branding and greeting-card options, apply quantity-tier pricing, split delivery across many recipient addresses, and output a clean branded quote and order sheet with a GST/BIR-ready invoice.

tools.title: Craft Workshop & Experience Booking Page
tools.problem: Experiences are a fast-growing craft income line but makers manage them over DMs with no slot booking, no deposit, no cap on batch size and no idea of the per-participant material cost, so sessions clash, no-show, or run at a loss.
tools.who: Artisans and studios who run paid hands-on experiences (pottery, block-print, weaving, bamboo, jewelry workshops) for tourists and hobbyists.
tools.solution: A workshop booking page: publish single and multi-session slots with a batch-size cap and skill level, collect a deposit via UPI/GCash, auto-compute the per-participant material-kit cost into the price, and manage the roster, reschedules and waitlist for each session.

tools.title: Craft Hangtag & Care-Label Studio
tools.problem: Products reach shelves with no professional swing tag or care label, and retail/packaged goods need statutory declarations (MRP, net quantity, manufacturer, country of origin) most makers omit, costing trust and risking non-compliance.
tools.who: Any artisan or craft brand putting products into retail, export or marketplaces.
tools.solution: A client-side tag designer: lay out print-ready swing tags and fabric/care labels with a QR to maker story, wash/care instructions and material composition, auto-insert the required Legal Metrology (India) or DTI (Philippines) declarations, and export a tiled PDF a local printer can run.
tools.regulation: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules 2011 (IN); DTI labeling rules (PH)

tools.title: Craft Order Material-Requirement & Reorder Planner (BoM)
tools.problem: When an order spans many designs, makers cannot quickly compute total materials needed (yarn, beads, clay, wood, findings, dyes), net it against stock on hand, and order the shortfall in time, so production stalls mid-order or over-buys.
tools.who: Craft units and cooperatives taking multi-design production orders against limited raw-material stock.
tools.solution: A material-requirement planner: define a bill of materials per design, enter the order's design quantities to explode total material demand, subtract current stock, and output a consolidated purchase list with per-material shortfall and lead-time flags.

tools.title: AERB eLORA Radiation Safety & TLD Dosimetry Register
tools.problem: Any medical X-ray installation must be registered/licensed on AERB's eLORA portal, each radiation worker needs a TLD badge with quarterly dose records, and QA tests and renewals fall due on schedules nobody tracks; lapses surface only when AERB issues a notice.
tools.who: Diagnostic X-ray, CT, mammography and dental-radiology centers, and their Radiation Safety Officers
tools.solution: A register of every X-ray machine with its eLORA registration/licence and expiry, a radiation-worker roster with quarterly TLD badge dispatch and dose-log, a QA/calibration schedule, and a 90/60/30-day due dashboard, plus a vault for the layout approval, RSO certificate and type-approval.
tools.regulation: AERB Radiation Safety (eLORA registration/licensing, TLD personnel monitoring, QA tests)

tools.title: Lab QC: Westgard Rules & Levey-Jennings Charts
tools.problem: ISO 15189 / NABL requires documented internal quality control, daily control runs plotted on Levey-Jennings charts, Westgard multirule interpretation and EQAS peer comparison, but small labs track this in error-prone Excel and collect non-conformities at assessment.
tools.who: NABL-accredited and NABL-aspiring clinical laboratories
tools.solution: Enter each analyte's control lot mean/SD, record daily QC values, and the tool auto-plots Levey-Jennings charts, applies Westgard multirules (1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s, 10x) to flag in-control vs reject runs, computes monthly CV and bias, and logs EQAS/PT results, producing the QC evidence file assessors ask for. Runs fully client-side so patient-adjacent data never leaves the lab.
tools.regulation: NABL / ISO 15189 (internal quality control, EQAS/PT participation)

tools.title: Ayushman PM-JAY Claim & TMS Document Packager
tools.problem: PM-JAY reimbursement runs through the TMS portal with pre-authorization, correct HBP 2022 package selection, mandatory document uploads and query responses; weak packages, wrong codes or missing documents cause rejections and months of blocked cash for a cash-strapped hospital.
tools.who: Small empanelled hospitals and nursing homes treating PM-JAY / state-scheme beneficiaries
tools.solution: A claim workspace that picks the right HBP 2022 package and rate, builds the pre-auth and final-claim document checklist (ID, diagnosis, implant invoice, discharge summary, outcome photos), tracks each case through pre-auth / query / approved / paid, and flags SLA breaches, so nothing is submitted incomplete and no query sits unanswered.
tools.regulation: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (NHA Health Benefit Packages 2022, TMS pre-auth/claim)

tools.title: Cashless Pre-Auth Desk & Insurance Receivables Tracker
tools.problem: Cashless cases pile up as unpaid TPA receivables for 60-120 days; pre-auths stall for missing documents, deductions and denials go uncontested, and no one knows which insurer owes how much or how old it is.
tools.who: Small hospitals, eye-care, dental and specialty clinics running TPA/insurer cashless
tools.solution: A desk that captures each cashless case with the hospital's Rohini details and PPN package, assembles the pre-auth and final-bill document set, then ages every claim by insurer/TPA with deduction and denial reasons, a resubmission clock, and a reconciliation of amount billed vs approved vs received.
tools.regulation: IRDAI health-insurance (cashless pre-authorization, Rohini hospital registry, PPN rates)

tools.title: Medical Device Dealer Licence & MD-42 Sales Record
tools.problem: Under the Medical Devices Rules 2017 device sellers now need a CDSCO sale licence (Form MD-42) and must keep purchase/sale records with batch and device details by risk class, plus handle recalls, a compliance burden most traders never had and can't track on paper.
tools.who: Wholesalers, distributors and retailers of medical devices (monitors, glucometers, surgical items, implants)
tools.solution: A licence vault (MD-42/MD-43 with expiry alerts), a device master tagged by risk class (A/B/C/D) and UDI/batch, purchase and sale registers capturing the statutory fields, and a recall/complaint log that traces which customers received an affected batch, the record-set a CDSCO inspection expects.
tools.regulation: Medical Devices Rules 2017 (CDSCO sale licence MD-42/MD-43, sale records, recall)

tools.title: Senior/PWD Medicine Discount Till & Purchase Booklet Register
tools.problem: Pharmacies must give senior citizens and PWDs 20% off plus VAT exemption on medicines, record each sale in the buyer's purchase booklet with their OSCA/PWD ID, and keep the separate register that supports the 20% as a BIR tax deduction; done by hand it is slow, error-prone and leaves money unclaimed.
tools.who: Drugstores, botika and pharmacy counters
tools.solution: A medicine till that computes the correct 20% discount and VAT-exempt price, prints the compliant sales slip, writes the purchase-booklet line (name, ID, medicine, quantity, signature), and maintains the SC/PWD sales register that rolls up into the monthly/annual deduction schedule the bookkeeper files with the BIR.
tools.regulation: RA 9994 (Expanded Senior Citizens Act) & RA 10754 (PWD): 20% + VAT exemption, BIR deduction

tools.title: PhilHealth eClaims All-Case-Rates Builder
tools.problem: Beyond Konsulta, facilities claim confinements and procedures under PhilHealth's All Case Rates using ICD-10 and RVS codes through eClaims; wrong code pairings, missing CF forms or incomplete data trigger return-to-hospital (RTH) and delayed reimbursement.
tools.who: Small hospitals, infirmaries, dialysis and surgical clinics filing PhilHealth confinement claims
tools.solution: A claim builder that maps the diagnosis and procedure to the correct ICD-10/RVS pairing and its case rate, validates the CF1/CF4 and member-eligibility data for completeness, flags common RTH reasons before submission, and exports the eClaims-ready package while tracking each claim from filed to paid.
tools.regulation: PhilHealth All Case Rates / eClaims (ICD-10, RVS codes, CF1/CF4, RTH rules)

tools.title: Dental Chair: Odontogram, Treatment Plan & Lab-Case Tracker
tools.problem: Dentists track tooth-by-tooth findings, treatment plans and per-procedure billing on paper, and separately lose track of crowns, dentures and aligners sent to the dental lab: which case is at try-in, which is overdue, which material and shade was ordered.
tools.who: Single- and multi-chair dental clinics
tools.solution: A clickable odontogram that records findings and planned/done procedures per tooth, generates the itemized treatment plan and estimate, bills per completed procedure, and runs a dental-lab case board (impression sent, due date, try-in, received, fitted) with material, shade and batch, so no lab case is forgotten and every tooth has a history.

tools.title: Optical Shop: Spectacle Rx & Lens-Lab Order Manager
tools.problem: Opticals jot the spectacle prescription (SPH/CYL/AXIS/ADD/PD) on slips, order lenses from a fitting lab verbally, and then can't tell a customer whether their glasses are ready, leading to errors, remakes and missed collections.
tools.who: Optical retail shops and optometry practices
tools.solution: Capture the prescription per eye with frame and lens choice (index, coatings, tint), generate the lab order with all parameters, track the job through ordered / at-lab / fitted / ready, SMS the customer when ready for collection, and keep the Rx and warranty on file for the next visit and remakes.

tools.title: Physiotherapy SOAP Notes & Package-Session Tracker
tools.problem: Physios sell multi-session packages but lose track of how many sessions a patient has used, under-document SOAP notes and outcome measures, and leak revenue when sessions aren't decremented or renewals aren't prompted.
tools.who: Physiotherapy, rehab and chiropractic clinics
tools.solution: Per-patient assessment (ROM, MMT, pain/outcome scores) with quick SOAP notes each visit, a package wallet that decrements sessions on attendance and flags when a package is exhausted or due for renewal, home-exercise plan sharing, and a therapist-wise utilization view.

tools.title: NAPS Apprentice Stipend & Reimbursement Manager
tools.problem: Apprenticeship paperwork (contract registration on apprenticeshipindia.gov.in, monthly attendance, stipend payment proof) and the government stipend-reimbursement claim are scattered across spreadsheets; one missing attendance or payment proof voids the reimbursement and establishments quietly lose money and drop apprentices.
tools.who: Third-party aggregators (TPAs), skilling providers and establishments running apprentices under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme.
tools.solution: A per-apprentice workspace that registers contracts, tracks the sanctioned trade and duration, records monthly attendance and stipend disbursement proof, computes the reimbursable share, and assembles the exact claim packet the DGT/portal expects, flagging any apprentice whose evidence is incomplete before the claim window closes.
tools.regulation: Apprentices Act 1961; National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS); DGT stipend reimbursement norms

tools.title: Descriptive Answer-Sheet Evaluation Workflow
tools.problem: Mains/descriptive evaluation is the hardest part of a test series: scanned booklets get mailed around on WhatsApp, evaluators grade inconsistently with no model-answer anchor, marks and feedback get lost, and students wait weeks, hurting the centre's reputation.
tools.who: UPSC/State-PSC, judiciary, banking-descriptive and board-exam coaching centres that grade handwritten subjective answers.
tools.solution: Booklets are scanned and auto-split by question; each question routes to the assigned evaluator with the model answer and rubric; annotations and per-criterion marks are captured; a second-evaluator/moderation pass reconciles outliers; the student gets an annotated copy plus topic-wise weakness analytics.

tools.title: Coaching Centre Registration & 2024-Guidelines Compliance Kit
tools.problem: The 2024 Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Centres (and state coaching laws) impose hard rules: no enrolment below age 16, mandatory qualified counsellor, prescribed refund on mid-course exit, infrastructure and fire norms; most centres have no idea what to file, display or enforce.
tools.who: Owners of private coaching and test-prep centres setting up or regularising under the new coaching-sector rules.
tools.solution: A guided builder that produces the registration document set, the mandatory policy pack (fee-refund policy, student-wellbeing/counsellor policy, code of conduct, disclosures), an age-16 enrolment gate for the admission register, and a state-tailored renewal/compliance checklist.
tools.regulation: Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Centre 2024 (Ministry of Education); applicable state Coaching Centres (Regulation) Acts

tools.title: TESDA Dual-Training & Enterprise-Based Training Manager
tools.problem: DTS/EBT programs split learning between school and company and carry strict paperwork (registered training agreements, in-plant training plans, the minimum 75%-of-wage trainee allowance, attendance across two sites, incentive/liquidation reporting) managed today in loose spreadsheets that fail TESDA monitoring.
tools.who: TVET providers and partner establishments running Dual Training System / Enterprise-Based Training programs.
tools.solution: A program workspace that registers each trainee's dual agreement, maps in-school vs in-plant competency hours, logs attendance at both sites, tracks the mandated allowance payments, and compiles the TESDA monitoring and incentive-claim reports.
tools.regulation: Dual Training System Act (RA 7686); TESDA Enterprise-Based Training rules; minimum trainee allowance (75% of applicable wage)

tools.title: LTO Driving-School TDC/PDC Course & Certificate Manager
tools.problem: No one can get a student permit without a 15-hour Theoretical Driving Course certificate, and practical-course hours and serial-numbered certificates are tightly controlled by the LTO; schools juggle enrolment, hour logs, instructor assignment and certificate issuance by hand and risk accreditation on any mismatch.
tools.who: LTO-accredited driving schools delivering the Theoretical and Practical Driving Courses.
tools.solution: Enrol students, schedule TDC/PDC sessions, log completed hours per module with instructor sign-off, issue serial-controlled TDC/PDC completion certificates with a QR verify, and keep the accreditation register (instructors, vehicles, course hours) audit-ready for LTO inspection.
tools.regulation: LTO driving-school accreditation; mandatory 15-hour Theoretical Driving Course (TDC) and Practical Driving Course (PDC) certification for licence applicants

tools.title: PRC CPD Provider Program & Unit Issuer
tools.problem: To give professionals the CPD units they need to renew PRC licences, a provider must get each program accredited, run it with compliant attendance, and issue participants the correct units with program/certificate numbers, a documentation load that blocks small providers from a lucrative recurring market.
tools.who: PRC-accredited CPD providers and training outfits seeking to award CPD units to licensed professionals.
tools.solution: A tool that assembles the CPD program accreditation application (learning objectives, resource persons, hours-to-units mapping) per profession, captures compliant attendance, and issues each participant a numbered CPD certificate with awarded units, plus the post-activity report PRC requires.
tools.regulation: Continuing Professional Development Act (RA 10912); PRC CPD Council provider accreditation and unit requirements

tools.title: Student Records Office: TC, Bonafide & Form 137/138 Generator
tools.problem: Issuing a Transfer Certificate, bonafide/good-moral certificate, or the Philippine Form 137 (permanent record) and Form 138 (report card) is slow, error-prone handwritten work with no serial control, so duplicates and lost records surface exactly when a parent urgently needs them.
tools.who: Small private schools, junior colleges and TVET centres issuing transfer certificates, report cards and official student records.
tools.solution: Maintain the student master and academic history, then generate serial-numbered TCs, bonafide/good-moral certificates, report cards and Form 137/138 from templates in the correct regional format, with a QR verify and an issuance register that prevents duplicates and reprints cleanly.
tools.regulation: State education-board Transfer Certificate rules (India); DepEd Form 137 (permanent record) and Form 138 (report card) (Philippines)

tools.title: Exam Seating Plan & Invigilation Roster Generator
tools.problem: Every exam day someone hand-draws seating arrangements (no two same-subject or same-class neighbours, within room capacity) and juggles invigilator duty allocation, hours of error-prone work repeated for each test, with mistakes causing chaos on the morning.
tools.who: Schools, colleges and coaching centres conducting in-centre exams and mock tests.
tools.solution: Import the candidate list and available rooms, auto-generate a conflict-free seating plan honouring capacity and adjacency rules, allocate invigilators fairly across rooms and slots, and print room charts, door lists, desk slips and the invigilation duty roster.

tools.title: Clash-Free Batch Timetable & Faculty-Load Planner
tools.problem: Scheduling many batches across a few rooms and shared faculty is a weekly headache: double-booked teachers, room clashes and uneven loads emerge by hand, and one change cascades into conflicts nobody catches until a class collides.
tools.who: Multi-batch coaching, tuition and skilling centres sharing limited classrooms and part-time faculty.
tools.solution: Define batches, subjects, rooms, faculty availability and weekly hour targets, then auto-build a conflict-free timetable, detect clashes on every edit, balance each teacher's load, and publish per-batch, per-room and per-faculty views the office and students can read.

tools.title: Admission Intake, Document Checklist & Merit-List Builder
tools.problem: Admission season is a flood of application forms and documents collected on paper and WhatsApp; verifying required documents, ranking applicants by marks/criteria, managing waitlists and seat allotment is manual, opaque and dispute-prone.
tools.who: Private schools, junior colleges, coaching centres and TVET providers running annual admissions.
tools.solution: A configurable admission form that collects applicant details and required documents against a checklist, verifies completeness, auto-builds the merit list by the chosen criteria (marks, category, preferences), manages waitlist and seat allotment, and issues offer/confirmation letters with a clean admissions register.

tools.title: CessClear — BOCW Labour-Cess & Worker Welfare Register
tools.problem: The 1% BOCW Welfare Cess and worker registration are widely misunderstood; contractors under-pay or skip the cess, never register workers with the State Welfare Board, and later face notices, interest and denial of worker benefits.
tools.who: civil contractors, developers and PMCs engaging construction labour
tools.solution: Go app: enter project cost / running-bill values, auto-compute the 1% BOCW cess per bill and cumulatively, maintain the statutory worker register (name, trade, Aadhaar, wages), generate the cess challan/return worksheet and the worker-registration form, and alert on payment due dates.
tools.regulation: BOCW Act 1996 & BOCW Welfare Cess Act 1996 (1% cess); State BOCW Welfare Board registration

tools.title: PCABGuard — License Renewal & Allowable-Range Bid Checker
tools.problem: Every bid needs a current PCAB license in the right category and size range; contractors miss renewals, mis-read their Allowable Range of Contract Cost (ARCC), and get disqualified or chase projects they are not licensed to take.
tools.who: PH general and specialty contractors (Small A/B, Medium)
tools.solution: Go app: stores the firm's PCAB category, classification and ARCC; before bidding, checks a project's Approved Budget for the Contract against the firm's allowable range and registration, tracks license/specialty-trade renewals and document expiry with reminders, and keeps the renewal document pack.
tools.regulation: RA 4566 (Contractors' License Law); PCAB license categories & Allowable Range of Contract Cost (ARCC)

tools.title: BatchSlip — RMC Dispatch & Mix-Design Log
tools.problem: Micro RMC plants dispatch concrete on handwritten slips with no link between the approved mix design, the m3 loaded per truck and the customer ledger; quantity/grade disputes are constant and QA records for audits are missing.
tools.who: small ready-mix concrete (RMC) plants and site batching operators
tools.solution: Go app: store approved mix designs per grade (cement, sand, aggregate, water, admixture per m3 to IS 10262 / ACI), issue a numbered dispatch slip per truck (grade, m3, slump, vehicle, time), roll up daily production and customer-wise m3 delivered, and keep the batch record for third-party audits.
tools.regulation: IS 10262 (mix proportioning), IS 4926 (RMC); PNS / ACI 318 for PH

tools.title: CubeLog — Concrete Cube Test Register
tools.problem: Cube sampling and 7/28-day compressive-strength testing is kept in loose registers; samples are forgotten at test age, strength trends are never computed, and the IS 456 acceptance criteria (mean + standard deviation) are checked by hand or not at all.
tools.who: site QA engineers, small testing labs, RMC plants, PMCs
tools.solution: Go app: register each cube set (ID, pour location, grade, casting date), auto-schedule 7- and 28-day test reminders, record crushing loads, compute compressive strength and running mean/standard deviation, apply the IS 456 (or ASTM C39) acceptance test, and print a stamped cube-test report per batch.
tools.regulation: IS 456 (acceptance criteria), IS 516 (testing); ASTM C39 for PH

tools.title: MatchMaterial — Theoretical-vs-Actual Consumption Reconciler
tools.problem: Cement and steel are the biggest spend and the biggest leakage; owners have no cheap way to know whether quantity consumed matches what the structure actually required, so over-ordering and theft go unnoticed until the budget blows.
tools.who: builders, PMCs and project owners worried about site pilferage
tools.solution: Go app: import theoretical requirements (steel from the BBS, concrete/cement from the BOQ and mix design) per structural element, enter actual material issued/received from challans, and flag any slab, floor or element where consumption exceeds theoretical plus an allowed wastage %, with a variance report by material.

tools.title: HoldBack — Retention, DLP & Bank-Guarantee Release Tracker
tools.problem: Retention (typically 5-10%) is deducted on every bill and released only after the Defect Liability Period; contractors lose track of how much is held, when each tranche is due, and when retention/mobilisation bank guarantees expire, leaving real cash un-chased.
tools.who: contractors and sub-contractors with money retained across projects
tools.solution: Go app: record retention deducted per bill per project, track the DLP clock and scheduled release dates, hold bank-guarantee details with expiry alerts, and produce a release-claim statement so the contractor can demand each tranche on time.

tools.title: HireMeter — Equipment Hour-Meter Rental Billing
tools.problem: Equipment is hired on hour-meter or shift basis with fuel, operator, idle time and shifting charges, but small rental owners bill from loose logsheets, lose hours, and argue with sites over idle-vs-working time and diesel.
tools.who: construction-equipment rental owners (excavator, JCB, crane, boom, roller)
tools.solution: Go app: log daily opening/closing hour-meter (or shifts) per machine per site with operator and diesel, separate working vs idle hours per the hire terms, and auto-generate the monthly rental invoice with fuel adjustment, shifting and tax — reconciled to the site's signed logsheet.
tools.regulation: GST on equipment rental (SAC 9973) / e-invoice where applicable; BIR for PH

tools.title: DealerDesk — Building-Material Counter Billing (Steel by Weight)
tools.problem: Generic retail billing does not fit a building-material counter: TMT steel sells by weight at a daily-changing rate, cement by brand at MRP, rods are cut to length, and most sales run on credit — so dealers bill on paper and lose on rate and credit control.
tools.who: cement, steel (TMT) and hardware dealers / building-material shops
tools.solution: Go app: catalogue with steel section unit-weights (bill by kg at today's rate from length/pieces), cement by brand/bag, cut-to-length rod sales, GST invoice (or BIR invoice for PH), and a per-customer running credit ledger with outstanding and reminders.
tools.regulation: GST tax invoice / e-invoice (India); BIR sales-invoice rules (PH)

tools.title: Contactless Guest Check-In & Digital Guest Register
tools.problem: Front desks still fill paper guest registers and photocopy IDs; the register is illegible, unsearchable, and a liability when police or municipal inspectors ask for a specific date's entries or a named guest's details.
tools.who: Small hotels, lodges, guesthouses and homestays (5-40 rooms) that must keep a police-inspectable guest register.
tools.solution: Guest scans a QR before arrival and self-fills a digital registration card (name, address, ID number, purpose, vehicle, stay dates) with an on-screen signature; the desk verifies, and the app keeps a searchable, tamper-evident register that prints in the local register format and exports any date range. Foreign guests are flagged and their data pre-filled for the separate Form C hand-off.
tools.regulation: State police lodging/guest-register rules (Sarais Act 1867 where applicable); Form C hand-off under Registration of Foreigners Rules

tools.title: Supplier Voucher & Service-Confirmation Issuer
tools.problem: Operators confirm suppliers over WhatsApp with no numbered voucher, so guests get turned away at a hotel that 'has no booking' and operators can't tie supplier invoices back to the service promised.
tools.who: Tour operators, DMCs and travel agents confirming hotels, transport and activities for booked guests.
tools.solution: Issue numbered service vouchers per supplier (guest names, dates, rooms/vehicle/activity, inclusions, billing instruction) as PDF/WhatsApp, let suppliers mark them redeemed, and track voucher-to-invoice payable status so every supplier bill maps to a voucher.

tools.title: Adventure Activity Waiver & Safety-Briefing Logger
tools.problem: Operators run risky activities on verbal consent or a photocopied form; when something goes wrong they can't prove the guest declared medical fitness, signed a liability waiver, or received the safety briefing, and insurers reject the claim.
tools.who: Trekking, rafting, diving, canyoneering, zip-line and other adventure-activity operators.
tools.solution: Each participant fills a medical self-declaration and emergency contact and signs a liability waiver on the guide's device offline, the guide logs the safety-briefing acknowledgement and instructor sign-off per trip, and every record is stored and exportable as a dated PDF pack for insurers.
tools.regulation: Ministry of Tourism Adventure Tourism Guidelines (India); activity/operator safety standards

tools.title: Wedding & Event Budget + Vendor Payment Tracker
tools.problem: Planners run each event across dozens of vendors with advances, balances and due dates in a spreadsheet; payments slip, client billing drifts from actual cost, and margin is unknown until it's too late.
tools.who: Wedding planners, event managers and banquet coordinators.
tools.solution: Per-event budget lines mapped to vendors with contracted amount, advance/balance and due dates; a payment calendar flags what's due, client billing is tracked against actual spend, and a live margin and cash-position view covers every running event.

tools.title: Warranty Claim & Dead-Part Return Reconciler
tools.problem: ASCs front labour and parts on in-warranty jobs and wait months for OEM reimbursement; the defective parts they owe back to the distributor go untracked and OEM credit notes are never matched to the claims raised, silently eroding cash.
tools.who: Authorized service centers doing in-warranty repairs for appliance, electronics and HVAC OEMs
tools.solution: Logs each warranty job with model/serial, labour and part claimed, links the defective-part return/dispatch (core/RMA) and the OEM claim ID, then reconciles OEM settlements and credit notes against submitted claims to surface short-paid, rejected and ageing claims on a recovery worklist.
tools.regulation: GST credit-note matching (CGST Sec 34); OEM warranty RMA

tools.title: AMC Pricing & Profitability Calculator
tools.problem: Firms price AMCs by gut, underprice comprehensive contracts, and discover only at year-end that parts and extra visits ate the margin.
tools.who: AMC operators (aircon, RO, lift, DG, fire, IT) quoting new annual contracts
tools.solution: Models a contract from its asset list, visit frequency, expected parts reserve, consumables, travel and technician cost; computes break-even price, margin at a target price, and a comprehensive-vs-non-comprehensive comparison; emits a branded AMC proposal with scope and SLA.

tools.title: Technician Visit Payout & Incentive Engine
tools.problem: Technician pay mixes base, per-visit rates, distance, spare-part sales commission and callback penalties; computing it in spreadsheets is error-prone and the disputes erode trust.
tools.who: Service firms paying field technicians per-visit, per-km and on parts/AMC commission
tools.solution: Define pay rules (per-visit by job type, distance slabs, parts/AMC commission %, callback/no-show penalties), auto-compute each technician's earnings from closed jobs, and issue a transparent payout slip the technician can read line by line.

tools.title: Service Callback & Rework Analyzer
tools.problem: A repair that fails again inside the warranty window means a free repeat visit — the single biggest hidden cost — but firms cannot see which technician, model or fault drives their callbacks.
tools.who: Service managers at appliance, HVAC and electronics repair firms
tools.solution: Links each new job to prior jobs on the same asset/customer, flags repeats inside a configurable callback window, and charts callback rate by technician, product model, fault code and spare part with a Pareto of root causes.

tools.title: Breakdown Ticket & SLA Desk
tools.problem: Breakdown complaints arrive on WhatsApp, calls and SMS, get lost, and clients later dispute whether the contracted response or resolution SLA was met.
tools.who: AMC and facility-service firms handling reactive breakdown complaints
tools.solution: One intake (WhatsApp/web/missed-call) opens a ticket with response and resolution SLA clocks pulled from the client's contract, auto-assigns and escalates on breach, captures the fix and CSAT, and reports SLA adherence per client for renewal reviews.

tools.title: Pest Control Treatment Log & License Guard
tools.problem: Operators must record exactly which pesticide, dose and batch was applied where, issue treatment certificates (especially anti-termite warranties) and keep their operator licence current — all on paper that fails audits and loses warranty claims.
tools.who: Pest-control operators (termite, general, fumigation, rodent) working on contracts
tools.solution: Per-contract treatment schedule; on-site log of chemical, concentration, batch and area treated; an auto-generated signed treatment certificate and warranty card; and licence-renewal alerts for the firm and its applicators.
tools.regulation: Insecticides Act 1968 / CIB&RC (IN); Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority (FPA) licence (PH)

tools.title: Lift License & Statutory Inspection Tracker
tools.problem: Each lift carries a state licence, a periodic statutory inspection and third-party insurance on staggered dates; miss one and the lift is illegal to run, but AMC firms juggle hundreds of them on spreadsheets.
tools.who: Lift and escalator AMC firms maintaining units across many buildings
tools.solution: Registers each lift with its building, licence number, inspecting authority, insurance and inspection cadence; rolls up due/overdue renewals per building, stores inspection reports and licence copies, and alerts the firm and building owner ahead of each deadline.
tools.regulation: State Lift Acts/Rules (e.g. Maharashtra Lifts Act; Karnataka / Tamil Nadu Lift Rules)

tools.title: DG Set Service & CPCB Emission Log
tools.problem: Genset AMC firms must track running hours for service plus emission/noise norms and the site's Pollution Control Board Consent-to-Operate — breaches now trigger CPCB action, yet the service logs live in notebooks.
tools.who: Diesel-generator AMC and O&M firms
tools.solution: Per-DG asset with running-hour and fuel logging, a service schedule by hours/months, emission-norm and retrofit (RECD) status, and SPCB Consent-to-Operate renewal tracking with document storage and alerts.
tools.regulation: CPCB DG-set emission norms (incl. RECD retrofit); SPCB Consent to Operate

tools.title: Legal Metrology Verification & Stamping Tracker
tools.problem: Every weighing and measuring instrument must be re-verified and stamped by Legal Metrology each year; a service firm managing hundreds of client instruments loses track of due dates and clients end up trading on illegal, unstamped scales.
tools.who: Weighbridge and weighing-scale sales and service firms
tools.solution: Registers each client instrument (type, capacity, serial, accuracy class) with its last verification/stamping date and jurisdiction, rolls up re-verification due dates, generates the verification worklist and reminders, and keeps a per-client register with certificate copies.
tools.regulation: Legal Metrology Act 2009 (periodic verification & stamping)

tools.title: Solar O&M & Generation-Shortfall Tracker
tools.problem: After install nobody watches whether the panels actually generate; dust, shading and faulty strings quietly cut output and owners blame the installer with no data.
tools.who: Rooftop-solar O&M providers and EPC firms offering post-commissioning service
tools.solution: Per-site expected-generation baseline (kW, tilt, local irradiance); logs monthly/inverter-read actuals, computes performance ratio and shortfall, schedules cleaning visits, and sends the owner an O&M and generation report that explains any underperformance.

tools.title: Garage Job Card & Emission-Test Reminder
tools.problem: Garages run on paper job cards, keep no service history and never follow up — so the customer's next service and lapsed emission certificate, and the repeat revenue, walk out the door.
tools.who: Two-wheeler and car repair garages
tools.solution: Digital job card with odometer, complaints, work done, parts and labour; per-vehicle service history keyed on registration number; and automatic next-service and emission-test (PUC / MVIS) expiry reminders over SMS/WhatsApp.
tools.regulation: PUC certificate under CMVR Rule 115 (IN); LTO MVIS emission test (PH)

tools.title: PH Electrical Permit & PEC Load Pack
tools.problem: Every electrical installation or alteration needs an LGU electrical permit with a PEC-compliant load schedule and a signing REE/PEE — and a rejected or mis-sized submission stalls the whole job.
tools.who: Philippine electricians and electrical contractors filing permits
tools.solution: Builds a PEC-compliant load schedule and panel-board schedule (load estimation, demand factors, conductor and breaker sizing, voltage drop), assembles the electrical-permit document set, and tracks the signing engineer and LGU approval status.
tools.regulation: Philippine Electrical Code 2017; RA 7920 (Electrical Engineering Law); LGU electrical permit

tools.title: FPO Patronage Bonus Calculator
tools.problem: Producer Companies must distribute surplus as patronage bonus tied to each member's transactions plus a capped limited dividend, a calculation that is tedious and error-prone by hand.
tools.who: FPO boards and accountants at year-end
tools.solution: Ingest member procurement/sales for the year, apply the patronage formula and limited-dividend cap, and produce a per-member distribution statement.
tools.regulation: Companies Act Part IXA distribution rules

tools.title: Coop Produce Order & Delivery Manager
tools.problem: The DA's Kadiwa program links coops directly to consumers and institutions, but coops run orders over tangled Facebook/Viber threads with no picking or settlement discipline.
tools.who: Farmer coops selling through Kadiwa and Sagip Saka
tools.solution: Publish a weekly produce catalog, take consumer and institutional orders, and auto-generate picking lists, delivery sheets and a collection summary.
tools.regulation: DA Kadiwa, Sagip Saka Act RA 11321 (LGU direct purchase)

tools.title: FPO Invoice + GST E-Invoice Bridge
tools.problem: When an FPO crosses the turnover threshold, B2B produce sales need a GST invoice with an e-invoice IRN and QR, which small FPO accountants find daunting.
tools.who: GST-registered FPOs selling to institutional buyers
tools.solution: Create produce lots and buyers, raise GST-compliant invoices, and obtain the IRN/QR via a GSP/NIC integration, with exempt-vs-taxable handling for agri goods.
tools.regulation: GST, e-invoice IRN (NIC/GSP), agri HSN exemptions

tools.title: e-NWR Warehouse Receipt & Pledge-Finance Manager
tools.problem: WDRA-registered warehouses must record graded commodity deposits and feed repositories (NERL/CCRL) to issue electronic negotiable warehouse receipts that farmers pledge for credit; small warehouses lack the system to do it cleanly.
tools.who: WDRA-registered rural warehouses and the FPOs depositing with them
tools.solution: Manage deposits, AGMARK grading, storage and the data needed to issue e-NWRs, plus a pledge-financing pack for the depositor's bank.
tools.regulation: WDRA, e-NWR (NERL/CCRL), AGMARK grading

tools.title: Crop-Insurance Premium & Claim Assistant
tools.problem: Smallholders miss crop-insurance enrollment windows, don't know their premium share, and fumble loss documentation, so claims fail.
tools.who: Farmers and FPO/coop enrollment helpers
tools.solution: Compute the farmer-share premium, track enrollment deadlines by crop and season, and on loss assemble the intimation and documentation pack.
tools.regulation: PMFBY (IN), PCIC (PH)

tools.title: Open-Cry Auction & Sale-Note Digitizer
tools.problem: Lots at mandis and FPO yards sell by open-cry auction recorded on paper, so bids, winners and sale notes are disputable and slow to settle.
tools.who: Mandi auction clerks and FPO sale yards
tools.solution: Run a simple ascending auction per lot on a tablet, record bids and the winning price, and instantly generate the sale note and settlement entry.
tools.regulation: APMC auction norms (IN), LGU market rules (PH)

tools.title: Scan-to-Pick Bin-Location WMS
tools.problem: Small warehouses track stock by memory and spreadsheet, pickers wander, and inventory goes 'missing' with no bin-level truth.
tools.who: Micro-3PL warehouses, D2C fulfilment centres and distributor godowns.
tools.solution: Print QR bin labels, scan with a phone to put away and to pick, and get real-time stock-by-location, pick lists and low-stock alerts; works offline and syncs.
tools.regulation: GST stock records (IN); general stock accountability.

tools.title: Returnable Asset (Pallet/Crate/Cylinder) Ledger
tools.problem: Pallets, crates, LPG cylinders and kegs go out and don't come back; MSMEs lose lakhs or pesos in unreturned assets with no ledger of who holds what.
tools.who: Distributors, beverage/dairy/LPG businesses and 3PLs.
tools.solution: An issue/return ledger per customer with QR-tagged assets, outstanding balance and aging per customer, and deposit tracking.
tools.regulation: GST-on-deposits note (IN).

tools.title: Carrier Compliance & Dispatch Gate
tools.problem: 3PLs and shippers onboard many small carriers and collecting/verifying RC, insurance, permit, PAN/TIN and bank details is chaotic, so expired documents slip through to active loads.
tools.who: 3PLs, brokers and shippers managing carrier panels.
tools.solution: A carrier self-upload portal with a document checklist and expiry tracking, verification status, and a dispatch gate that blocks tendering loads to a non-compliant or expired carrier.
tools.regulation: GST, insurance, permit (IN); LTFRB franchise, LTO registration (PH).

tools.title: Failed-Delivery (NDR) Re-Attempt Manager
tools.problem: Last-mile non-delivery reports (customer not home, wrong address, COD refusal) are handled ad hoc, so re-attempts and RTO pile up and kill margins.
tools.who: D2C sellers, courier resellers and 3PLs.
tools.solution: Capture the NDR reason at the doorstep, auto-send the customer a confirm link (reschedule / confirm COD / correct address), queue the re-attempt, and auto-decide RTO after N failures.
tools.regulation: BSP e-wallet COD confirmation (PH).

tools.title: Scan-Verified Pick List & Packing Slip
tools.problem: Small fulfilment packs straight from a printout of raw orders, causing mis-picks and missing items with no verification step.
tools.who: D2C sellers, e-commerce sellers and micro-3PLs.
tools.solution: Import orders (CSV or marketplace export), generate wave pick lists and packing slips, scan each item to verify it's packed, and print shipping labels.
tools.regulation: None.

tools.title: Returns & RTO Grading Intake
